content: Polyethylene glycol-electrolyte solution (PEG-ES) is a medication used to thoroughly cleanse the bowel prior to gastrointestinal procedures such as examinations or surgeries. It achieves this by inducing diarrhea. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes, so it is important to consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional details. This medication is provided as a powder that must be mixed with water to create a solution for oral consumption. The solution should be prepared according to the instructions provided on the label. Once prepared, an 8-ounce glass of the solution should be consumed quickly every 10 minutes until the prescribed volume has been ingested or until your stool becomes watery, clear, and free of solid material. Your doctor will specify the time at which you should begin drinking the solution. It is essential to avoid eating for at least 3 to 4 hours before starting the medication. Additionally, you should not take any oral medications within one hour of beginning PEG-ES. Bowel movements typically begin within one hour of starting the solution. Follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not deviate from the prescribed dosage or frequency. Before using PEG-ES, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any allergies to this medication or other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins and herbal supplements, that you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you have a history of gastrointestinal diseases or obstructions. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, discuss this with your doctor before taking PEG-ES. Mild side effects of PEG-ES may include an upset stomach, abdominal pain, bloating, vomiting, or rectal irritation. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects, such as a rash, hives, or skin irritation, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a serious adverse reaction, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program either online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, ensuring it is tightly sealed and kept out of reach of children. Once the solution is mixed, it should be stored in the refrigerator and used within 48 hours. Discard any unused or expired medication. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. It is important to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and any required laboratory tests. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. This medication is available under the brand names CoLyte® and GoLYTELY®.
